topic: Revolt of 1857 — leaders and centres — mixed tiers
description: Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, Tatya Tope, Bahadur Shah Zafar — centres and outcomes

questions.stem: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:

options.option_text: Meerut (Bengal Army sepoys mutinied; marched to Delhi the next day)

questions.explanation: 10 May 1857 — sepoys of the Bengal Army's 3rd Light Cavalry refused to use the new Enfield rifle cartridges (rumoured to be greased with cow + pig fat). 85 imprisoned sepoys had been court-martialled the previous day. Massive mutiny on 10 May; sepoys + civilians attacked British officers in Meerut, then marched ~70 km south to Delhi overnight, declaring Bahadur Shah Zafar (the last Mughal) as Emperor of Hindustan on 11 May. Mangal Pandey's earlier incident at Barrackpore (29 March 1857) is sometimes called the proximate trigger.

questions.stem: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting British troops on:
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai (originally Manikarnika Tambe; m. Raja Gangadhar Rao) — born 19 November 1828 in Varanasi. After her husband's death (1853), Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse refused to recognise her adopted son Damodar Rao. She joined the Revolt — defended Jhansi (March-April 1858 against Hugh Rose), retreated to Kalpi, then to Gwalior. Died fighting in male warrior attire at Kotah-ki-Sarai on 17/18 June 1858 — age 29. Gen Hugh Rose called her 'the bravest and best of the rebel leaders'. Subhadra Kumari Chauhan's poem 'Khoob Ladi Mardani' immortalised her.

questions.stem: Match the centre of the 1857 Revolt with its leader — INCORRECT pairing:
questions.explanation: Bihar/Arrah was led by KUNWAR SINGH (the 80-year-old zamindar of Jagdishpur). Tatya Tope (Ramachandra Pandurang Tope) led the Kanpur + Gwalior campaigns alongside Nana Saheb. Other 1857 centres: Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar (figurehead), General Bakht Khan (military leader); Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal (regent for Birjis Qadr); Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah; Allahabad — Liaqat Ali; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Mathura — Devi Singh.

questions.stem: After the 1857 Revolt was suppressed, control of India was transferred from the East India Company to the British Crown by:

options.option_text: Government of India Act 1858 + Queen Victoria's Proclamation (Allahabad, 1 November 1858)

questions.explanation: Government of India Act 1858 — abolished East India Company. Power transferred to Crown. New post: Secretary of State for India + 15-member Council of India to assist. Governor-General became 'Viceroy' as well — Lord Canning, the first. Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1 November 1858, read out by Canning at Allahabad) — promised: religious tolerance, no further annexation by Doctrine of Lapse, equal treatment for Indians regardless of caste/creed/colour, recognition of treaties with princes. Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled to Rangoon, died 1862. Mughal Empire formally ended.

questions.stem: Mangal Pandey — sepoy whose actions on 29 March 1857 are considered a precursor to the Revolt — was executed at:
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey — 34th Bengal Native Infantry sepoy at Barrackpore. On 29 March 1857, attacked Lt Baugh + Sgt Hewson over the Enfield cartridge issue + general resentment. Was overpowered, court-martialled, hanged on 8 April 1857 — 10 days earlier than scheduled, fearing public unrest. His unit (34th BNI) was disbanded. The reverberations contributed to the May 1857 Meerut incident. Often hailed as 'first martyr of Indian independence struggle'. Hindi film 'Mangal Pandey: The Rising' (Aamir Khan, 2005). Birthday celebrated as 'Shaheed Diwas' in his hometown Nagwa, UP.

questions.stem: The principal cause of immediate sepoy outrage was the introduction of the Enfield rifle. The greased cartridges were rumoured to contain:

options.option_text: Tallow from cow (offending Hindus) and pig fat (offending Muslims)

questions.explanation: Enfield Pattern 1853 rifle — required biting open paper cartridge before loading; cartridge was greased with animal fat. Rumour spread that the grease was a mix of cow tallow + pig fat — abhorrent to Hindus (cow sacred) AND Muslims (pig haram). The Company tried to mitigate (use unsalted/tallow-free, use teeth alternative — bite less etc) but rumour had spread. Larger underlying causes: economic distress, Doctrine of Lapse annexations (Awadh 1856), missionary activity, treatment of Indian soldiers. The cartridge was the spark, not the cause.

questions.stem: V.D. Savarkar's 1909 book 'The Indian War of Independence — 1857' was significant because it:

options.option_text: Was the first British account of the Revolt
Recast the 1857 events as a planned 'first war of independence' rather than a sepoy 'mutiny'

questions.explanation: Savarkar's 'The Indian War of Independence — 1857' — written in Marathi 1908; published in English 1909 from London (where he was a law student); banned by British. Recast 1857 as the first organised, premeditated nationalist uprising against British rule (a major shift from the British framing of 'sepoy mutiny'). Influenced later nationalists. Other major historians of 1857: R.C. Majumdar (cautious — argued events were diverse, not centrally coordinated), S.N. Sen (1857), Eric Stokes, Tapti Roy, Rudrangshu Mukherjee. Surendra Nath Sen's centenary government work (1957) is balanced.
